$comment: Experiment T7, sub-phase 3.7. Which typeface a run is drawn in when the named one is absent, and how absence is detected in a browser. Written by tools/ground-truth/fonts/substitution/analyse.ts.

units.width: thousandths of a point, from TextRange2.BoundWidth
units.advance: thousandths of a CSS pixel, from OffscreenCanvas.measureText

questions.question: What does PowerPoint draw a Latin face it does not have in?

scores.name: the style word in the name

questions.question: Do @panose, @pitchFamily and @charset change what an absent face becomes?
Is an absent face laid out with the substitute own metrics, or scaled?
questions.answer: The substitute own, exactly: every reading equals Calibri to the last digit.

questions.question: Which collection do +mj-lt and +mn-lt name?
questions.answer: +mj-lt is a:majorFont/a:latin and +mn-lt is a:minorFont/a:latin, substitution applied after.

scores.name: major to majorFont, minor to minorFont

questions.question: Does TextRange2.Font.Name report the requested face or the drawn one?
questions.answer: The requested face, after theme resolution and before substitution.

questions.question: How is an absent family detected in the browser?
questions.answer: By measuring it stacked on all three generics: absent means equal to every one of them.

scores.name: the bare family differs from the browser default
